text.p: Here are highlights of stories reported by Hungary's press, based on information by Nepszabadsag's Hungary Around the Clock service. For further details on how to subscribe to Hungary Around the Clock, please contact Monica Kovacs at (361) 351 7142 or fax your request to (361) 351 7141.
***GENERAL***
ALL PAPERS
- Four opposition parties and three farmers' unions propose a referendum against a planned land law amendment which would enable foreigners to buy farmland in Hungary.
- Leader of opposition party Young Democrats said in an interview that his party supports authonomy for ethnic Hungarians in Romania.
- An official of opposition party Democratic Forum warned that half of Hungary's population lives in a crisis region by EU standards.
- The head of the Parliamnet's foreign affairs committee said regular Horn-Meciar meetings are essential.
- Ethnic Hungarians from Slovakia have appealed to Hungarian Prime Minister Gyula Horn to help improve their situation.
NEPSZABADSAG
- Israeli Prime Minister Benjanim Netanyahu will visit Hungary between September 19 and 21.
***BUSINESS***
ALL PAPERS
- Hungary's foreign trade deficit in the first six months of 1997 was $1.145 billion.
- Producer prices in June rose 0.8 percent month-on-month and 19.4 percent year-on-year.
- The january-July central budget deficit was 188.9 bilion forints.
- Audi will start to produce eight-cylinder engines in its Gyor plant in the second half of the year.
NEPSZABADSAG
- The commercial director of Hungary's state television joined the private TV consortium MTM-SBS, owners of one national TV channel franchise.
VILAGGAZDASAG
- The Budapest Bank privatisation will bring the state 14.8 billion forints of profits by the year 2001, a Finance Ministry study shows.
